official_measurement_examples.name: Current Approved Document P
official_measurement_examples.fact: The current GOV.UK Approved Document P is the 2013 edition for electrical safety in dwellings and explains design, installation, inspection, testing and notification of work.

official_measurement_examples.name: Part P commencement history
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government circular 05/2004 records that the original Part P provisions came into force on 1 January 2005, subject to transitional provisions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Competent person route
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK states registered competent-person installers can self-certify specified building work instead of the customer obtaining separate building-regulations approval for that work.

official_measurement_examples.name: Completion evidence timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current GOV.UK guidance says a registered tradesperson using the competent-person route should provide a compliance certificate within 8 weeks of completion.

official_measurement_examples.name: Third-party certification route
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance states registered third-party certification schemes have been available for domestic electrical work undertaken by others since 6 April 2014.

official_measurement_examples.name: Typical notifiable work
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current local-authority guidance identifies new circuits, consumer-unit replacement and additions or alterations in special locations as examples of electrical work requiring notification unless a valid self-certification route applies.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 competence framework
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Building Safety Regulator and MHCLG published a mandatory technical competence framework for self-certification schemes on 1 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK building-regulations guidance explicitly states building regulations approval is different from planning permission and a project can require both.
